title: XIII-XVI: efficient, impulsive, material causes
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): or two principles with ye Manichees, wander out from ye truth — those who invent eternal matter with Aristotle. for creation stands as out from nothing. Matter properly so called did not lie beforehand toward created things; or ye love by means belonging toward that same which God willed to communicate His good outwardly — but ye impulsive cause belonging toward creation stands as Gods communicative goodness. XIV. but also no creature can create — nor stands as creation belonging toward all things efficiently out from God alone only. XIII.
pass_b_english: XIII. Nor is creation of all things efficiently from God alone only, but also no creature can create. XIV. But the impulsive cause of creation is Gods communicative goodness, or the love by which God willed to communicate His good outwardly.

Matter properly so called did not lie beforehand for created things; for creation is from nothing. Those who invent eternal matter with Aristotle, or two principles with the Manichees, wander from the truth.
source_text: XIII. Neque tantum est rerum omnium efficienter creatio a solo Deo, sed et nulla creatura creare potest. XIV. Impellens vero creationis causa est bonitas Dei communicativa, seu amor quo Deus bonum suum ad extra communicare voluit. Materia proprie dicta rebus creatis non praejacuit; creatio enim est ex nihilo. Qui materiam aeternam fingunt cum Aristotele, aut duas principia cum Manichaeis, a veritate aberrant.
